SWMA 302(A) - DISPOSAL, PROCESSING AND STORAGE OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person disposed, processed, stored, or permitted the disposal, processing or storage of residual waste in a manner which is contrary to the rules and regulations of DEP or to any permit or to the terms or conditions of any permit or any order issued by DEP.
properties.content:
Report Details
Operator: William H Brawand
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 2019-10-04
Violation Code: SWMA 302(A) - DISPOSAL, PROCESSING AND STORAGE OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person disposed, processed, stored, or permitted the disposal, processing or storage of residual waste in a manner which is contrary to the rules and regulations of DEP or to any permit or to the terms or conditions of any permit or any order issued by DEP.
Violation ID: 864250
Permit API: 047-24421
Unconventional: No
County: Elk
Municipality: Jones Twp
Inspection Type: Complaint Inspection
Inspection Date: 2019-10-04
Comments: This inspection was performed following the Department receiving a complaint of possible brine dumping in a ditch line near the Brawand 53 well location. This inspection was performed with WQSS Rich Sheriff. The well is equipped with an electric powered pumpjack, and appears to be producing. The stuffing box seems to have leaked at times, as there is a coating of oil on the wellhead and ground. The well is tagged and the access road and site are stable. There is a ditch line/UNT to Johnson Run that flows near the entrance to this site. The ditch flows to the southeast and into a small pond approximately 500 feet away, which has an outlet to continue down-gradient. A check with a handheld conductivity meter and probe shows elevated levels in this channel immediately around a culvert and at various spots flowing downstream. There is also evidence of tree and other vegetative death along the immediate banks of this UNT, indicating that brine was likely discharged into this channel. (See attached photos) The Operator may contact WQSS Rich Sheriff at 814-723-0973 to discuss this incident.

Permit API: 065-25518
Unconventional: No

Inspection Date: 12/12/2023
Comments: This site located west off Odonnell Road, 1 1/2 miles south of railroad crossing on State Game Lands Road, at the end of second branch to the north. Well is set-up for production with a meter, separator and one tank in secondary containment. Tank has been removed from site. A report of a release of 32 gallons of produced water was reported by Will Warfel with Diversified Prod LLC at 12:30 on 9/21/23 at this well site. The release was assumed to be from the separator, there is an area of no vegetation around the well head, separator and meter and a path 70x15' path to the west. WQS Taylor received notification from Heather Empfield that Moody and Associates Inc were to be employed to sample this site to determine the extent of the contamination. Contaminated soil has been removed from end of path of dead vegetation to the west. Based on conductivity testing, completed on October 24, 2023 at an onsite meeting with Lisa Raffle, Wil Warfel and Paul Stiner, there is brine contaminated soil near the well head and secondary containment around the tank, on the stabilized parking area and in all areas of dead vegetation from the original notification of a release on site. Stone has been placed on the initial uphill section of the access road, partial stabilization has been completed. Access is still muddy and rutted, should be stabilized. This well is on Exhibit A of the Diversified Consent Order and Agreement and shows no annual production.

properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: BLACKHILL ENERGY LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 7/29/2024
Violation Code: 78a56(a) - TEMPORARY STORAGE - Operator failed to contain regulated substances and wastes used at or generated at a well site in a tank, series of tanks or other storage structures approved by the Department.
Violation ID: 8196390
Permit API: 015-21167
Unconventional: Yes
County: Bradford
Municipality: Smithfield Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 7/29/2024
Comments: The Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted an incident inspection at Blackhill Energy's Nichols A (1H) well site located in Smithfield Township, Bradford County on 7/29/2024 at 1120 hours. The weather was 77 degrees F with mostly clear skies. The inspection was conducted in response to a discovered release reported by the operator. Complaint Tracking System (CTS) ID #382564 is tied to this release within CTS.On 7/29/2024 at ~0815 hours, Blackhill Energy discovered a produced water release to the pad surface at their Nichols (A) well site. The release appeared to come from a water truck after or during recovering water from the produced water tank onsite. Blackhill Energy is unsure of the total amount of the release. Moody and Associates, Fenton Transport/Trucking, and Blackhill Energy representatives were all present during my visit. During my inspection, the overview of the release area was observed. Some portions of the pad surface within the release area were damp but no standing or pooled water was present in the area. White colored staining and/or crystals were observed in the area. Soil within the area of the release was field measured for electrical conductivity (EC) with a Hanna Groline Soil Conductivity Meter and returned a reading of >4.0mS/cm (photo #4). Soils within the stormwater channels along the edges of the pad were field measured for EC below 1.0mS/cm. All other soils, pad materials and pooled water field measured on the pad surface, outside of the release area were field measured for EC below 1.0mS/cm. No evidence was observed that would suggest any portion of the release escaped the outlined release area. Blackhill Energy reported that the release would have occurred when a water truck was offloading from the produced water tank onsite on 7/27/2024. It was believed that foam from the produced water was able to escape from the vent on the side of the truck. A waste container for impacted material was en route to the site when I departed. Excavation activities were set to begin upon arrival of the waste container.Based on the findings of this inspection report and the reported release of an unknown quantity of produced water outside of secondary containment, violations of the following are cited against API #015-21167 at this time:35 P.S. 691.402(b)25 Pa. Code 78a.56(a)35 P.S. 6018.301I departed the site at 1215 hours.

Comments: This inspection was conducted as a follow-up to the incident that occurred during the frac on October 11, 2020 when the operator reported that diesel was released to the pad. The frac is complete and three wells are currently in flowback. The site secondary containment and rig mats have been removed from the pad. A representative from Falcon, contractor for Chesapeake, was present on the pad. The area of the pad impacted by the release appears to have been backfilled with new gravel. The electrical conductivity of the puddles in this area was between 500 to 800 uS/cm. No sheens were observed in any of the puddles. No staining was observed anywhere on the pad. The excavated material which had been staged on containment during the incident inspection on October 13, 2020 has been removed. Violations remain outstanding. The operator indicated in their NOV response received via email by the Department on October 27, 2020 that they would pursue Act 2 remediation. The outstanding violations will be closed once attainment with Act 2 standards has been confirmed.

properties.content:
Report Details

Violation Code: SWMA 301 - MANAGEMENT OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person operated a residual waste processing or disposal facility without obtaining a permit for such facility from DEP. Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
Violation ID: 904126
Permit API: 003-22470
Unconventional: Yes
County: Allegheny
Municipality: Forward Twp
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 1/06/2021
Comments: This inspection is taking place as a follow up to IR 3129333 which documented an operator reported release of fluid from a GPU to the ground on 12/23/2020. The following is observed: The Act 9 sign is present and appears to be in good condition (Photo 1). The ERP, PPC, and associated safety data sheets are present in the mailbox. The GPU's do not appear to be in secondary containment (Photo 2), per the COA signed on 12/17/2020, this is being noted as ICS. The sump is still present adjacent to the GPU (Photo 3), conductivity readings taken in and around the sump read in the 60-70 uS range. Based on the on-site conditions, the site does not appear to have been remediated. Mr. Lance Witters with EQT was spoken to by phone, he confirmed that the site is still being remediated under 78a.66c(1). Mr. Witters was advised that under the previsions of 91.33(B) the site should be remediated by no later than 1/7/2020. Mr. Witters stated that a follow up by the operator will be conducted to evaluate the remediation effort. No migration of impacted material to stormwater management facilities or WOTC is observed. The roll off box with impacted material is still present on the pad (Photo 4). Based on this inspection violations noted in IR 3129333 remain outstanding. Pending a follow up inspection, more violations may be forthcoming. The Department requests the waste manifest once it is available.

Report Details
Inspection Client: RANGE RESOURCES APPALACHIA LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety

Violation ID: 8271849
Permit API: 007-20655
Unconventional: Yes
County: Beaver
Municipality: Independence Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 4/20/2026
Comments: On 4/20/2026, the Department conducted an inspection in response to a spill at Minton William well pad in Independence Township, Beaver County. The spill reportedly occurred on 3/31/2026, at 4:15 PM. The spill was reportedly caused when a minor surge of gas caused produced water to release from the casing of well 11H to the graveled well pad, while the operator conducted work on well 11H. An estimated 10 gallons of produced water released and was contained to the graveled well pad. The operator reportedly remediated this release in accordance with 78a.66(c)(1). The operator reported the spill to the Department on 3/31/2026, at 5:11 PM (IR 4172810). Accompanying the Department during this inspection is Range Resources representative Nate Smiell. Intermittently present was Range Resources representative Derek Zofchak. The Erosion and Sedimentation Control General Permit (ESCGP) for this site was terminated on 10/13/2021.The following was observed during the inspection:The Act 9 sign is installed at the entrance of the access road and is not obscured from view by vegetation, in accordance with 78a.55 (photo 1). The Emergency Response Plan (ERP), Preparedness Prevention and Contingency (PPC) plan, and new well permits are on site (photos 10-13). The ERP and PPC plan appear to contain the sections required by 78a.55. Eight gas wells are onsite that appear to be equipped for production (photo 16). Well 11H is temporarily shut-in to accommodate the drill rig (photo 18). Smiell reported that well 13H is being drilled at the time of inspection (photo 8). The production tanks and the surrounding secondary containment appear to be sound at the time of inspection (photo 4). The GPU/Vertical Separator Units are equipped with interconnected secondary containment drip pans (photos 5 and 6). This form of GPU secondary containment was approved by the Department for use on 6/21/2022. All other storage containers and machinery on site that appear to contain regulated substances are placed within secondary containment (photos 9 and 14). The secondary containments on site appear to be in good condition at the time of inspection, with no observable holes or tears. No evidence of fluid releases, such as staining, was observed on the well pad surface during this inspection. The containment inspection log is available on site in the company trailer (photo 17). The access road and well pad appear to be stable at the time of inspection with no observable concerns relating to accelerated erosion and sedimentation (photos 2 and 3).Based on observations from this inspection, violations shall be noted and immediately corrected against the 3/31/2026 spill.

Municipality: West Keating Twp

Comments: The weather was 42 Deg. F and windy at the time of inspection. Follow up inspection of Frontier Natural Resources, Winner Pad, well # 1 April 27, 2022, regarding Inactive Well Status application received by the Department. The Winner # 1 was drilled in 2008 and has not been produced to date; the well was granted Inactive Status for a period of five years beginning on 8/21/2013. Inactive Status expired for the Winner # 1 on 8/21/2018. One annulus vent (production x intermediate casing) was observed at the Winner #1 gas well. The annulus vent was monitored for combustible gas using a MSA Altair 5X; 100% LEL and 100% Methane was detected at the annulus vent during the inspection. Since most recent inspection by an OGI, company operator partially removed gravel from inside the cellar to get a better view of the gas bubbling source. Observed gas bubbling inside the surface and intermediate annular space at the high rate at time of inspection. There is no production equipment on site. No new violations were noted during this inspection, but there are three continuous outstanding violations, that have been previously filed. Frontier Natural Resources Representatives - Biru Sarkar, Production Engineer; Jon Miller, General Manager. DEP Representative - Ulyana Trynovich, Oil and Gas Inspector.

properties.content:
Report Details

Violation Date: 5/03/2023
Violation Code: SWMA 302(A) - DISPOSAL, PROCESSING AND STORAGE OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person disposed, processed, stored, or permitted the disposal, processing or storage of residual waste in a manner which is contrary to the rules and regulations of DEP or to any permit or to the terms or conditions of any permit or any order issued by DEP.
Violation ID: 993566
Permit API: 047-25052
Unconventional: Yes
County: Elk
Municipality: Jones Twp
Inspection Type: Complaint Inspection
Inspection Date: 5/03/2023
Comments: This is a complaint inspection following a report by the operator of a large production water spill at this site on 4/26 at 7:30 am. An initial site visit was performed by WQSS Rob Bechtel. This inspection was performed with Seneca's Jeff Passerello.The initial spill occurred when a cast iron gate valve failed as the operator was pumping production water to a stimulation operation on the E09-U pad. The pump was in operation at 50 barrels per minute. The operator was able to stop the leak eventually. Water spread out across the northern edge of the site, entering a perimeter ditch. It then ran around the edge ditch of the site and eventually entered an infiltration berm on the southwest corner of the location. The operator brought in a pump and was able to collect a significant amount of liquid from this location. The operator's estimate is that 1500+ barrels of produced water was released. The operator has scraped up ~150 tons of material from the surface of the location and staged it on site to remove to the landfill. A pump is placed and the operator is using it to pump water collecting in the berm into tanks on site. Water does not appear to have passed the berm at this time, at least superficially. The operator has brought in ARM Group to do an initial analysis of the site and to take samples for removal to the landfill. Further inspection on this site will be done as necessary as cleanup continues.

Comments: On 12/17/2024 a representative from the Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted a follow-up inspection of Greylock Production LLC's Ron multi-well pad located in Hector Township, Potter County. Upon arrival to the site at 1000 hours, weather was 45F and sunny. An Act 9 sign and well permits are visible and located at the site entrance (photo #1).Hydraulic fracturing activities remain ongoing onsite and are estimated to be completed near the end of next week. Equipment to support well stimulation remain onsite and all equipment which is required to be held in containment was observed in secondary containment structures (photos #2-6)This inspection was conducted in response to a release of produced fluids from secondary containment reported by Greylock on 12/13/2024 at 0245 hours (CTS #385788). The cause of the release was determined to be a hydraulic fracturing pump which leaked produced fluids that accumulated and overtopped from secondary containment; the release has been contained. Contaminated material was already removed and backfilled by my arrival onsite (photo #7). The soil in this area field measured for electrical conductivity (EC) at ~40us/cm. Standing fluids were observed near the area of the release and field measured for EC at ~1140us/cm. Two vacuum trucks for removing fluids have been stationed onsite and were sent to remove the fluids from this area. Greylock took corrective action after this release and rebuilt the entire containment berm and rig-matting system with an 18-inch wall for increased capacity and to prevent additional releases (photo #8).The low points of the produced fluids offload containment structure which was the site of the release on 12/09/2024 (Inspection Report #3881391) have been repaired and a pump has been installed to continuously remove fluids from this containment structure as they accumulate (photos #9-11).The drainage system which was conveying fluids and diesel into the site's infiltration basin on 12/09/2024 (Inspection Report #3881391) remains shut in and a pump has been installed to remove accumulating fluids. No fluids were observed entering the basin at the time of this inspection (photo #12). Contaminated materials have not yet been excavated from the basin as per my previous recommendation to follow Act 2 remediation guidelines (photo #13).The DEP recommends the following:-Continuing to remove fluids as they accumulate in secondary containment structures.-Continue following Act 2 remediation requirements for the ongoing remediation efforts onsite, including those set to take place in the infiltration basin.-Continuing daily secondary containment inspection.No additional violations noted at this time. The violations noted in inspection report #'s 3881391 and 3878285 remain outstanding against API #105-21962.I departed the site at 1100 hours.

Equipment to support well stimulation remain onsite and all equipment which is required to be held in containment was observed in secondary containment structures (photos #2-6)This inspection was conducted in response to a release of produced fluids from secondary containment reported by Greylock on 12/13/2024 at 0245 hours (CTS #385788). The cause of the release was determined to be a hydraulic fracturing pump which leaked produced fluids that accumulated and overtopped from secondary containment; the release has been contained. Contaminated material was already removed and backfilled by my arrival onsite (photo #7). The soil in this area field measured for electrical conductivity (EC) at ~40us/cm. Standing fluids were observed near the area of the release and field measured for EC at ~1140us/cm. Two vacuum trucks for removing fluids have been stationed onsite and were sent to remove the fluids from this area. Greylock took corrective action after this release and rebuilt the entire containment berm and rig-matting system with an 18-inch wall for increased capacity and to prevent additional releases (photo #8).The low points of the produced fluids offload containment structure which was the site of the release on 12/09/2024 (Inspection Report #3881391) have been repaired and a pump has been installed to continuously remove fluids from this containment structure as they accumulate (photos #9-11).The drainage system which was conveying fluids and diesel into the site's infiltration basin on 12/09/2024 (Inspection Report #3881391) remains shut in and a pump has been installed to remove accumulating fluids. No fluids were observed entering the basin at the time of this inspection (photo #12). Contaminated materials have not yet been excavated from the basin as per my previous recommendation to follow Act 2 remediation guidelines (photo #13).The DEP recommends the following:-Continuing to remove fluids as they accumulate in secondary containment structures.-Continue following Act 2 remediation requirements for the ongoing remediation efforts onsite, including those set to take place in the infiltration basin.-Continuing daily secondary containment inspection.No additional violations noted at this time. The violations noted in inspection report #'s 3881391 and 3878285 remain outstanding against API #105-21962.I departed the site at 1100 hours.

No equipment associated with the plugging of the well or the plugged well site was observed at this time. Based on today's inspection, violations are being issued for failure to have the site restoration plan on site. Comments: On August 19, 2026, the Department conducted a complaint inspection of the Cecil 2-P229 OG Well in regard to CTS 400392.The findings are as follows:At the time of the inspection, the Department did not observe an Act 9 sign. The Department recommends the operator install an Act 9 sign in accordance with 78a55. The Department also did not observe an Emergency Response Plan (ERP). The Department recommends the operator ensure an ERP is onsite in accordance with 78a55.At the time of the inspection the well was located in an open agricultural field. The access road appeared stabilized. No erosion or sedimentation issues were observed at the time of the inspection.Upon inspection of the production equipment, the well appeared equipped for production. A well tag and well posting were present onsite appeared to have all information in accordance with OGA3211(G) and OGA3211(H). There were no observed leaks or discharges of fluid at the surface around the wellhead.There appeared to be 3 total production tanks onsite. Upon further inspection, it appeared the white poly tank was connected and in use. The tank appeared to be in sound condition with no observed leaks or discharges of fluid were observed around this tank.Two metal tanks were also present onsite but did not appear to be in use at the time of the inspection. Upon further inspection of the 2 metal tanks, one of the tanks appeared to be severely corroded with multiple holes in the tank observed. The Department observed fluid flowing down the side of the tank. A conductivity reading of this fluid was obtained and was "OR" (Over detectable range, >20mS). Upon inspection of the ground surrounding the corroded production tank, the Department observed orange staining and saturated dirt/gravel. Conductivity readings were taken in the area of staining and saturation with readings of 12.78mS, 9.24mS, 4.37mS, and 1.82mS being obtained. These readings are elevated in comparison to the background conductivity reading obtained of 0.19mS. Based on the Department's observations and conductivity readings, it appears a release has/is occurring from the corroded production tank.Prior to leaving the site, the Department spoke with operator representative Robert Inghram and informed him of the Department's observations of an apparent release. Mr. Inghram stated the metal tanks have been disconnected and empty for several years. The Department recommended remediation of the spill and removal of the production tanks as they are no longer in use and heavily corroded. Mr. Inghram stated he would get a contractor to begin the work as soon as possible.Based on today's inspection, violations are being issued for the observed release, production equipment onsite not in use, no ERP onsite, and no Act 9 Sign onsite.

A battery of frac tanks is present within secondary containment. The tanks and containment appear to be in good condition. Violations remain outstanding.

Unconventional: No

Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 12/27/2023
Comments: December 27 2023, the Department conducted a follow up inspection in regards to the spill reported to the Department on 10/20/2023 (CTS: 375673). According to the operator, the spill was approximately 40 barrels of production fluid, released from the valve near the bottom of the production tank. The initial inspection of the spill is documented in IR 3636824. The findings are as follows:At the time of the inspection, the production tank appeared to be removed from the site and it appeared that excavation of the contaminated material had begun. The area of excavation was approximately 30 feet by 30 feet and roughly 5.5 feet in depth. The Department took conductivity readings at the bottom of the excavated area with readings of 0.02mS, 0.12mS, and 0.18mS. It appeared that all of the excavated material was still on site, in several piles surrounding the excavated hole. In some areas, it appeared sediment had begun to travel downslope from the piles. Upon further inspection, it appeared that no E and S BMPs were implemented anywhere on the site. The Department recommends the operator promptly install E and S BMPs to prevent further migration of sediment and to minimize the potential for further sedimentation to occur.Based on today's inspection, violations are being issued for failure to implement E and S BMPs to minimize the potential for accelerated erosion and sedimentation. Previous violations associated with the release remain outstanding.

Comments: On 5/30/2023, DEP representative John Rogers conducted a routine site inspection at the Chesapeake Stoorza well site. It was 74 degrees and clear when I arrived on location. No E and S issues were observed during the time of the inspection. The site appeared stable and well vegetated, meeting the 70% uniform, perennial, vegetative cover. PCSM is addressed by three retentive grading/infiltration areas that are adequately stabilized and functioning as designed.There were two wells staged for production. Both wells were tagged with API/well permit numbers. No bubbling within the cellars was observed. The GPUs and production tank had secondary containment. A gas compressor is on site but was not running during the inspection.An inspection conducted by the department on 3/30/2023 described three waste piles of excavated material transported from the Chesapeake Grippo well site that had been temporarily stored at this location. Report Details

Violation Date: 3/29/2022
Violation Code: CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
Violation ID: 959040
Permit API: 081-21885
Unconventional: Yes
County: Lycoming
Municipality: McIntyre Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 6/09/2022
Comments: An incident inspection was conducted in response to a notification from the operator that a release of an estimated 5 barrels of produced water occurred which then overflowed secondary containment during completion operations on Pad B. I met with Rick Hall of EQT upon arriving on location. According to Mr. Hall, a hose failed which was hooked up to a booster pump that was being used for coiled tubing operations at the time of the release. After the secondary containment overflowed, the produced water flowed toward the stormwater channel along the pad edge. Mr. Hall said that he would have a sump dug in the stormwater channel at the pad edge to attempt to recover as much of the release as possible. Due to the amount of equipment on the pad and the waterlines and electrical cables along the side of the pad, Hall said that little excavation would be possible until completion operations were finished. He said that completions may be done as soon as the middle of July. He also said that Creston Environmental was en route to conduct screening of the site. Due to the volume of fluid which was released from the failed hose and the unknown volume of fluid released to the pad surface, the Department recommends pursuing Act 2 remediation. Violations remain outstanding for the March 29, 2022 release on Pad B.
